;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] agrees to hand over control of [[Yarmouk Camp]] in southern [[Damascus]] to the [[Syrian Army]] in return for safe passage to ISIL-held territory in the [[Syrian Desert]], bringing the predominantly [[Palestinian refugees|Palestinian refugee]] district under government control for the first time since 2012. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle_east/islamic-state-group-to-give-up-last-pocket-in-syrian-capital/2018/04/20/61001278-448b-11e8-b2dc-b0a403e4720a_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[International military intervention against ISIL]]
**[[Iraq]] conducts a series of air strikes against an [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] target in [[Syria]]. [https://www.yahoo.com/news/iraq-bombs-isis-apos-terrorist-210548506.html (Yahoo! News)]
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**Palestinians riot along the Israel-Gaza border fence, burning tyres and flying flaming kites across the border to set Israeli fields ablaze; [[Israel Defence Forces]] soldiers respond with tear gas and live fire, killing four Palestinians, including a 15-year-old, according to the [[Hamas]]-run health ministry. [https://www.haaretz.com/middle-east-news/palestinians/gaza-march-of-return-protests-continues-for-fourth-consecutive-we-1.6013144 (''Haaretz'')] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/palestinians-say-gazan-killed-by-idf-sniper-fire-near-border/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[B’Tselem]] alleges Israeli forces have been firing on tents around 400 metres back from the border housing protestors including the elderly and children, and attacked peaceful protestors with [[tear gas]]. [https://www.btselem.org/gaza_strip/20180419_military_fires_tear_gas_at_gaza_protest_tents (B’Tselem)]
**One petrol bomb-carrying kite is flown over the border adorned with a [[swastika]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/palestinians-fly-swastika-kite-with-petrol-bomb-across-gaza-border-into-israel/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[First Liberian Civil War]]
**[[Liberia]]n warlord [[Mohammed Jabbateh (Jungle Jabbah)|Mohammed "Jungle Jabbah" Jabbateh]] is sentenced to 30 years in prison in the [[United States]] for [[immigration to the United States|immigration]] offences. Jabbateh lied to authorities about his role in the Liberian Civil War. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-43836567 (BBC News)]
*[[Russia]]n [[frigate]] ''Yaroslav Mudry'' passes through the [[English Channel]], and is shadowed by [[Royal Navy]] coastal defence ship [[HMS St Albans|HMS ''St Albans'']]. [https://nypost.com/2018/04/20/royal-navy-tails-russian-warship-amid-rising-tensions/ (''The New York Post'')]
* [[2014–2018 Nicaraguan protests]]
** The government put the number of people killed in two days of protests at 10. [https://www.thenational.ae/world/the-americas/ortega-cancels-reforms-after-24-reportedly-die-in-nicaragua-protests-1.723868 (''The National'')]

;Arts and culture
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**Actress [[Natalie Portman]], who was born in [[Jerusalem]], pulls out of the upcoming [[Genesis Prize]] (worth 1 million USD) ceremony in [[Israel]] over "recent events in Israel". The [[Genesis Prize Foundation]] says it is worried the event will become politicised. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/natalie-portman-israel-genesis-prize-ceremony-palestinian-gaza-protests/ (CBS News)]
*[[Expo 2020]]
**[[Tajikistan]] announces that it will participate in the [[Expo 2020]] in [[Dubai]]. [https://en.trend.az/casia/tajikistan/2891010.html (Trend)]
*[[Deaths in 2018]]
**[[Sweden|Swedish]] musician [[Avicii]] dies in [[Oman]] at the age of 28. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43841194 (BBC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economy of the United States]]
**[[Wells Fargo]] bank is fined [[United States dollar|US$]]1 billion by the United States government for mishandling of mortgages and automobile loans. Wells Fargo is also ordered to reimburse customers who were overcharged. [http://money.cnn.com/2018/04/20/news/companies/wells-fargo-regulators-auto-lending-fine/index.html (CNN)]
**All [[The Bon-Ton|Bon-Ton]] department stores are expected to close by August. At the time of announcement, the company operated 256 stores under its own name and the [[Bergner's]], [[Boston Store (Wisconsin)|Boston Store]], [[Carson's]], [[Elder-Beerman]], [[Herberger's]] and [[Younkers]] nameplates. [https://www.pymnts.com/news/retail/2018/bon-ton-store-closings/ (Pymnts.com)] [http://money.cnn.com/2018/04/19/news/companies/bon-ton-liquidation/index.html (CNN)]
*[[South Korea]]n shipbuilding firm [[Sungdong]] collapses into receivership after surviving on government aid for eight years. [https://splash247.com/sungdong-shipbuilding-officially-placed-court-receivership/ (Splash 24/7)]

;Disasters and accidents
*Around 40 people are injured after two passenger trains collide in [[Salzburg]], [[Austria]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-austria-crash/about-40-slightly-injured-in-austrian-train-accident-police-idUSKBN1HR0I5https://www.reuters.com/article/us-austria-crash/about-40-slightly-injured-in-austrian-train-accident-police-idUSKBN1HR0I5 (Reuters)]
*Around 10,000 people are evacuated from central [[Berlin]], [[Germany]], while [[bomb disposal]] experts defuse a {{convert|500|kg|lb}} [[World War II]]–era British bomb at a construction site. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43833138 (BBC News)]
*[[Mount Iō (Shiretoko)|Mount Iō]] in northern [[Japan]] erupts for the first time in 250 years, together with nearby [[Mount Kirishima]] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/weather/2018/04/20/japanese-volcano-mount-io-erupts/535232002/ (''USA Today'')] [http://clicklancashire.com/2018/04/19/volcano-erupts-in-kyushu.html (''Click Lancashire'')]
*[[Southwest Airlines Flight 1380]]
**The [[United States]] [[Federal Aviation Administration]] issues an emergency [[Airworthiness Directive]] for [[CFM56-7B]] jet engines. The EAD expands on previous orders requiring [[ultrasonic testing]] to search for [[metal fatigue]] in fan blades. It mandates testing on engines that have reached 30,000+ flights<!--"flight cycles" in aviation jargon used by the source-->, believed to cover 352 US engines and 681 engines worldwide. [http://avherald.com/h?article=4b798bcf&opt=0 (The Aviation Herald)] [http://avherald.com/h?article=4b7725fb&opt=0 (The Aviation Herald)]
*A helicopter crashes in [[Sulawesi]], [[Indonesia]], killing one and injuring nine. [http://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/one-dead-nine-injured-in-sulawesi-helicopter-crash (''The Straits Times'')]

;Health and environment
*A [[United Kingdom|British]] man reported last month to be suffering what doctors called the "worst-ever" super-[[gonorrhoea]] is said by [[Public Health England]] to have been cured. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-43840505 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[2017–18 North Korea crisis]]
**[[North Korea]] [[Supreme Leader (North Korean title)|leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]] announces that North Korea will suspend its [[List of North Korean missile tests|missile]] and [[List of nuclear weapons tests of North Korea|nuclear]] tests and has agreed to shut down its nuclear test sites. [https://www.military.com/daily-news/2018/04/20/north-korea-suspends-missile-tests-closing-nuclear-test-site-report.html (Military)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/north-korea/north-korea-says-it-has-suspended-nuclear-missile-testing-n867961 (NBC News)]

;Law and crime
*[[List of offenders executed in the United States in 2018|Offenders executed in the United States in 2018]]
**[[Alabama]] executes 83-year-old [[Walter Moody]] via lethal injection, who assassinated [[United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit]] judge [[Robert Smith Vance]] on December 16, 1989. Moody is the oldest prisoner to be executed in the US since the death penalty was reinstated by the Supreme Court in 1976. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-43836864 (BBC News)]
*[[Cybercrime]]
**The [[Central Criminal Court (England and Wales)|Central Criminal Court]] in [[London]] jails Kane Gamble, 18, for two years for unlawfully accessing [[CIA]], [[FBI]] and [[United States Department of Justice]] databases and phone and email accounts of senior US intelligence officials. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-leicestershire-43840075 (BBC News)]
*[[Politics of Zimbabwe]]
**The [[Parliament of Zimbabwe]] summons ex-[[President of Zimbabwe|President]] [[Robert Mugabe]] over an alleged theft of [[diamonds]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-43839068 (BBC News)]
*[[Basque conflict]]
**The [[Basque separatism|Basque separatist]] terrorist group [[ETA (separatist group)|ETA]] apologises to "every victim" of its actions. The ETA killed more than 800 people in its 40-year history, committing terrorists attacks throughout [[Spain]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-43834750 (BBC News)]
*[[Crime in Poland]]
**A court in [[Radom]], [[Poland]], hands a six-month suspended prison term and a 10,000 [[polish zloty|zloty]] fine to a [[Russia]]n pilot who caused a security scare during [[Pope Francis]]'s 2016 visit for [[World Youth Day]]. The Russian had flown from the [[Czech Republic]] to compete in an international aerobatics competition and unknowingly violated a no-fly zone imposed for the papal visit. After failing to contact the aircraft, local authorities scrambled two [[F-16|F-16 fighter jets]] to intercept it. [http://www.thenews.pl/1/9/Artykul/359890,Penalty-for-Russian-pilot-who-triggered-alert-during-papal-visit-to-Poland (Radio Poland)]
**[[Poland|Polish]] Justice Minister and Prosecutor General [[Zbigniew Ziobro]] announces plans for a change to national [[self defence]] law to allow people to use more force than their attacks, and orders prosecutors to abandon proceedings against a businessman who shot at a getaway car containing fleeing robbers. [http://www.thenews.pl/1/9/Artykul/359850,Justice-minister-wants-immunity-for-people-who-defend-themselves (Radio Poland)]
*The [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Department of Justice]] announces it intends to appeal yesterday's ruling that an unnamed detained [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] suspect in the custody of U.S. troops in [[Iraq]] cannot be transferred to an unnamed foreign nation. The man has dual U.S.-[[Saudi Arabia]]n citizenship. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/19/politics/isis-citizen-transfer/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Inn Din massacre]]
**A [[Myanmar Police Force|Myanmar police]] captain testifies in court that he and his colleagues were ordered by their superiors to [[Entrapment|entrap]] two [[Reuters]] journalists, who were arrested on 12 December 2017 for "possessing state secrets" under a colonial-era law. The journalists had been working on a report documenting the massacre at [[Inn Din]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-journalists/myanmar-police-set-up-reuters-reporters-in-sting-police-witness-idUSKBN1HR12Q (Reuters)] [https://www.voanews.com/a/myanmar-policeman-testifies-arrested-reporters-were-set-up/4358822.html (Voice of America)]
*An [[Iraq]]i judge hands a [[capital punishment|death sentence]] to an [[ISIL]] member who acted as a judge deciding on marriages in [[Mosul]]. [http://www.kurdistan24.net/en/news/881012d5-e116-4f69-a981-58e4067255f1 (Kurdistan 24)]

;Politics and elections
*''[[Democratic National Committee v. Russian Federation]]''
**The [[Democratic National Committee]] file a lawsuit against [[Russia]], the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Donald Trump administration]], and [[WikiLeaks]] alleging that the former conspired to [[Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections|interfere in the 2016 United States elections]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/democratic-party-files-lawsuit-alleging-russia-the-trump-campaign-and-wikileaks-conspired-to-disrupt-the-2016-campaign/2018/04/20/befe8364-4418-11e8-8569-26fda6b404c7_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Brexit negotiations]]
**The [[UK]] [[National Audit Office (United Kingdom)|Audit Office]] rejects a [[HM Treasury|Treasury]] estimate of the cost of leaving the [[European Union]] that was repeated by [[UK Prime Minister|Prime Minister]] [[Theresa May]]. Rather than the official [[pound sterling|£]]35–39 billion estimate, the watchdog says that figure misleadingly included £7.2 billion earmarked directly for private hands and did not include up to £3 billion in budget contributions and £2.9 billion in [[European Development Fund]] payments. [https://www.fxstreet.com/news/uk-audit-office-brexit-divorce-bill-to-exceed-gbp-39bn-201804200312 (FXstreet)]
*[[2018 United States gun violence protests]]
**On the anniversary of the [[Columbine High School massacre]], thousands of students across the [[United States]] walk out of school to protest against school shootings. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/hundreds-school-walkouts-planned-friday-n867726 (NBC News)] [http://people.com/crime/national-walkout-day-anniversary-columbine-massacre-protest-gun-violence/ (''People'')]

;Science and technology
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**A study has been revealed that [[WASP-104b]], a [[hot Jupiter]] [[exoplanet]], has been discovered as one of the darkest exoplanets ever seen. [https://www.newscientist.com/article/2167030-distant-jupiter-like-world-may-be-the-darkest-planet-ever-found/ (''New Scientist'')]
